newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke sees continued buoyancy in London.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke sees continued buoyancy in London.

text.p: Ladbroke's London hotels should continue to benefit from buoyant economic conditions in 1997, said chairman John Jackson at a news conference.

"London is still buoyant and we do not expect any deterioration this year," he told reporters. The company owns either fully, or in part, 36 hotels in Britain, 10 of them in London, including the flagship five star London Hilton in Park Lane.
Thirty hotels are expected to join the jointly owned Hilton Corp and Labroke reservation system over the next four years.

"The main room we can grow our results is to increase the room rate. We have put in further increases for 1997 which are holding... but times are still very tough in France and Germany," said Jackson.
The recent strength of sterling against other European currencies has not had much impact on occupancy as yet, executives told the news conference.
But finance director Brian Wallace said the company expected to take a hit of 7 to 8 million stg in 1997 if current sterling exchange rates prevail.
